title: Biological approach: chemical messengers and genes
summary: How neurotransmitters, hormones and pheromones influence behaviour, how far behaviour is inherited, and the diathesis-stress model.

keyterms.definition: A chemical released across a synapse that passes a signal from one neuron to another, e.g. serotonin, dopamine, acetylcholine.
The gap between neurons across which neurotransmitters travel to bind to receptors.
A substance that increases or mimics the action of a neurotransmitter.
A substance that blocks or reduces the action of a neurotransmitter.
A chemical secreted by glands into the bloodstream that affects target organs, e.g. cortisol, oxytocin.
A chemical released outside the body that may affect the behaviour of others of the same species.
The proportion of variation in a trait within a population that can be attributed to genetic differences.
Comparing concordance between identical (MZ) and non-identical (DZ) twins to estimate genetic influence.
The percentage of twin pairs in which both twins show the same trait or disorder.
A disorder develops when a predisposition (diathesis) combines with environmental stress.
Changes in whether genes are expressed, caused by environment, without changes to the DNA sequence.

questions.prompt: Antonova et al. (2011) gave participants scopolamine before a spatial memory task. What does scopolamine do?
questions.explanation: Scopolamine blocks acetylcholine receptors; it reduced hippocampal activation during memory encoding.

questions.prompt: Kosfeld et al. (2005) gave men intranasal oxytocin or a placebo before a trust game. Result?
options: Oxytocin increased the money investors entrusted to a human trustee
Oxytocin increased risk-taking against a computer
questions.explanation: Oxytocin increased trust in people but not general risk-taking with a computer.

questions.statement: Hormones travel in the bloodstream, whereas neurotransmitters act across synapses.
questions.explanation: This is why hormonal effects are usually slower and longer-lasting.

questions.statement: Wedekind et al. (1995) found women preferred the smell of T-shirts worn by men with MHC genes similar to their own.
questions.explanation: They preferred men with dissimilar MHC genes, except women taking the contraceptive pill, whose preference reversed.

questions.text: A drug that blocks a neurotransmitter's receptors is an ___.
questions.explanation: Agonists enhance, antagonists block.

questions.text: Crockett et al. (2010) found that boosting serotonin with citalopram made participants more averse to causing ___ in moral dilemmas.
questions.explanation: Raising serotonin increased harm aversion, showing a neurotransmitter influencing moral judgement.

questions.prompt: Match each chemical messenger to its type.

pairs.right: Hormone linked to trust and bonding

questions.explanation: Some chemicals (like oxytocin) act as both hormones and neurotransmitters.

questions.prompt: Newcomer et al. (1999) gave participants high doses of cortisol for four days. What happened to verbal declarative memory?
options: It was impaired, then recovered after the drug stopped
questions.explanation: High cortisol, like chronic stress, impaired memory; the effect was reversible.

questions.prompt: Why is research on human pheromones controversial?
options: A specific human pheromone has not been reliably identified
questions.explanation: Findings like Wedekind's are interesting but often hard to replicate, and no human pheromone is confirmed.

questions.prompt: Order the steps of synaptic transmission.
items: Action potential reaches the axon terminal
Neurotransmitter is released into the synapse
Neurotransmitter binds to receptors on the next neuron
Neurotransmitter is reabsorbed or broken down
questions.explanation: Reuptake ends the signal; SSRIs act by blocking serotonin reuptake.

questions.prompt: In twin studies, genetic influence is suggested when:
options: DZ concordance is higher than MZ
MZ concordance is higher than DZ
questions.explanation: MZ twins share about 100% of genes and DZ about 50%, so higher MZ concordance points to genetic influence.

questions.prompt: Bouchard et al. (1990) studied twins reared apart. They estimated that about how much of the variance in IQ was genetic?
questions.explanation: The Minnesota study estimated about 70%, though the sample was self-selected and twins often had similar environments.

questions.statement: A heritability of 0.4 means 40% of a person's depression is caused by genes.
questions.explanation: Heritability describes variation in a population, not how much of one individual's trait is genetic.

questions.statement: Caspi et al. (2003) found people with short 5-HTT alleles were more likely to become depressed only if they had experienced many stressful life events.
questions.explanation: This gene–environment interaction supports the diathesis-stress model.

questions.text: In the diathesis-stress model, the inherited vulnerability is called the ___.
questions.explanation: The diathesis only leads to a disorder when combined with stress.

questions.text: Weaver et al. (2004) found that rat mothers' licking and grooming changed gene expression in pups, an example of ___.
questions.explanation: Cross-fostering showed the care, not the birth mother, changed stress-related gene expression.

questions.prompt: Match each study to its contribution.

pairs.right: Maternal care changed gene expression in rats

questions.explanation: Together these show genes matter but interact with the environment.

questions.prompt: Kendler et al. (2006) estimated heritability of major depression in a large Swedish twin sample. They found it was:
options: Higher in women than in men
Higher in men than in women
questions.explanation: Estimates were around 40% for women and around 30% for men, so environment also plays a large role.

questions.prompt: A key limitation of twin studies is:
options: Twins share environments, so genetic and environmental effects are confounded
questions.explanation: MZ twins may be treated more alike than DZ twins, inflating heritability estimates.

questions.prompt: Order the diathesis-stress pathway proposed by Caspi et al. (2003).
items: Person experiences several stressful life events
questions.explanation: Neither the allele nor stress alone predicted depression strongly; the combination did.
